hero.description: Welcome. I build the bridge between the rigor of software and the complexity of the physical world. I design high-performance architectures and advanced control systems, where precision is not an option, but the standard.

about.title: About Me
about.subtitle: From Hardware to Cloud: Engineering Reliability
about.p1: I am a Computer Engineer who graduated with honors from <1>Politecnico di Torino</1>, where I am currently specializing in <3>Automation and Intelligent Cyber-Physical Systems</3>. My goal is to design systems where software rigor meets the complexity of the physical world, ensuring performance, security, and scalability.
about.p2: I have cross-functional experience ranging from <1>real-time control</1> on embedded systems (ARM Cortex-M3), to developing high-performance <3>distributed systems</3> in <5>Rust</5> and WebAssembly, up to designing <7>full-stack IoT</7> architectures. I don't settle for code that "just works": I seek maximum efficiency and robustness.
about.p3: I tackle complex challenges by applying solid mathematical and control foundations: from developing Deep Learning (<1>LSTM</1>) models for predictive safety in collaborative robotics, to synthesizing <3>Feedback Linearization</3> laws in <5>MATLAB</5> for autonomous vehicle fleets.
about.p4: I look up to mission-critical standards of entities like <1>NASA and ESA</1>. I firmly believe that every memory allocation, network protocol, or control loop must be engineered to guarantee fault tolerance and absolute reliability. I am ready to bring this mindset and my technical skills to challenging and innovative corporate projects.

iot.title: IoT & Smart Home Automation Developer | Full-Stack Project
iot.desc: I engineered a distributed home automation system, focusing on interoperability between different technologies and protocols (MQTT, HTTP). I developed a scalable backend with CherryPy for the dynamic management of users and resources, integrating Arduino nodes for advanced environmental monitoring. The project stands out for the implementation of contextual automation algorithms: the system autonomously analyzes noise and movement levels to optimize the operation of lights and ventilation, guaranteeing granular control both via CLI interfaces in Python and via physical feedback on LCD displays.

dsp.title: Spectral Analysis and Digital Filter Design (MATLAB)
dsp.desc: I developed a digital signal processing system in MATLAB for spectral analysis and audio filtering. I implemented algorithms for the calculation of the FFT and designed low-pass and high-pass FIR filters (based on sinc function and Dirac delta), validating their performance through the calculation of the transfer function. The system was optimized and tested both on real audio tracks and on Gaussian white noise to guarantee the accuracy of the frequency response and the effectiveness of the attenuation.

gol.title: Development of the Analytic Engine and Persistence for an advanced Conway’s Game of Life simulator (Java & JPA)
gol.desc: In this project I designed and implemented the Board module, the structural heart of an extended version of the Game of Life. I dealt with the management of the grid and the dynamic interaction between the cells and the environment, implementing calculation systems for energy modifiers and 'life points'. A central aspect of my work was the development of a robust analytical engine capable of extracting real-time statistics and time series on the evolution of the simulation, using the Java Stream APIs. I also managed the entire persistence layer through JPA/Hibernate, mapping complex relationships between entities and guaranteeing the saving and restoration of the complete state of the board on an H2 database.

arm.title: Embedded Systems & Real-Time Control: ARM Cortex-M3
arm.desc: For the Computer Architectures and Systems course, I developed a real-time system based on ARM Cortex-M3 that runs an advanced version of Tetris on a LandTiger board (LPC1768). I integrated speed control via analog signals (ADC) and hardware audio playback, implementing optimized algorithms for handling collisions, power-ups and dynamic malus. The project, implemented in C with Keil IDE, demonstrates my ability to make complex software algorithms dialogue with physical hardware in resource-constrained contexts.

hrc.title: Predictive Safety & Dynamic Risk Estimation in Human-Robot Collaboration
hrc.desc: This project focuses on proactive safety for human-robot collaboration (HRC) in the industrial sector. The main objective was to create a system capable not only of detecting proximity in real time, but of actively predicting the evolution of the collision risk. Using the 3D kinematic data of the CHICO dataset, we implemented a deep learning architecture in two phases: an MLP network for instantaneous evaluation and an LSTM model for temporal forecasting. Thanks to advanced data augmentation strategies and a strictly safety-first optimization, the framework is able to anticipate collisions guaranteeing a fail-safe intervention. The result is a robust and proactive solution, essential for ensuring the control and reliability of modern intelligent cyber-physical systems.

formation.title: Distributed Formation Control of Heterogeneous Nonlinear Planar Robots via Feedback Linearization
formation.desc: The work addresses the challenge of distributed control for a team of three heterogeneous nonlinear planar robots, operating as Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASV). The primary objective was to ensure the maintenance of a rigorous triangular formation during the tracking of a spatial trajectory. To overcome the dynamic differences between the vehicles, a hierarchical architecture was implemented: an inner Feedback Linearization loop compensated for local nonlinearities transforming the system into double integrator linear models, supported by a Luenberger observer for the estimation of unmeasurable states. On this virtual plant, two high-level cooperative control protocols were designed and compared: one based on State-Feedback (via Riccati equation) and one based on frequency Loop-Shaping. The effectiveness of the architecture was validated through MATLAB simulations, demonstrating high stability and disturbance rejection even in severe marine scenarios characterized by wind gusts, sensor noise and parametric uncertainties.

rust.title: Georuggine: Distributed System in Rust for Fleet Geolocation
rust.desc: Academic project developed in Rust for the management, geolocation and real-time communication of a vehicle fleet. The system is based on a distributed client/server architecture, exploiting full-duplex communication via WebSocket to ensure continuous tracking on the map of Turin. The asynchronous backend, engineered with Axum and Tokio, interfaces with a SQLite database to analyze telemetry, while the motion simulator exploits a road graph elaborated in Python and is executed in the browser thanks to WebAssembly (WASM). Validated through concurrent stress-tests to ensure minimum latency and minimum impact on resources.
